the forward backward algorithm does not always lead to optimal parameter values for speech recognition, that the corrective training procedure is an alternative estimation procedure aimed at maximizing recognition accuracy, and that it can lead to significant improvements over conventional estimation methods.

the forward backward algorithm is a good way to estimate the parameters of hidden Markov models for speech recognition, but that the parameters estimated via this algorithm do not necessarily lead to the maximum possible recognition accuracy.

the forward-backward algorithm is a good way to train hidden Markov models and that it is better to use the maximum mutual information criterion to train hidden Markow models than to use the maximum likelihood criterion.

the problem of estimating the parameters of hidden Markov models in a way which is most appropriate for speech recognition.
the problem of finding the parameter values which maximize recognition performance.
the problem of estimating the values of the parameters of hidden Markov models for speech recognition.

the corrective training procedure leads to better recognition accuracy than conventional training methods, and that it is a useful alternative to maximum likelihood estimation.

, for the particular speech recognition system that was used in the experiments, and for the particular set of training and testing data, corrective training leads to fewer errors than does conventional maximum likelihood training.

it is not always appropriate to estimate model parameter values by maximizing likelihood.
